result:
Two findings. I'd fix the typo and decline the rounding change, because D2 settles it.

**Finding 1 (Minor, typo).** The docstring typo is real. It changes no behavior, so there is no RED test to write. `make test` is the check that nothing broke.

**Finding 2 (Important, ROUND_HALF_UP).** I would not implement this. The plan's D2 is an owner decision from plan review (2026-11-02): round half-even, to match the ledger system. The reviewer's reason, that customers expect half-up, is an outside opinion that contradicts that recorded decision, and the reviewer may not have seen D2. Reversing it is the owner's call, not a code-review fix. It isn't one of the five stops, so I'd record a ruling, keep going, and put the question in my message to the partner.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

If it passes, I'd append the ledger lines and commit in one call:

<command>
cat >> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md <<'EOF'
Final review fix pass: fixed docstring typo "neerest" -> "nearest" in rates/card.py (no behavior change, no RED test applicable; make test green).
Ruling: declined final-review finding "switch round_price() to ROUND_HALF_UP" — plan Decision D2 (owner, 2026-11-02) requires ROUND_HALF_EVEN to match the ledger system, and the spec is the binding authority — if wrong, customers who expect half-up see exact-half prices rounded to the even cent, and the fix is a one-line change plus tests for the tie cases.
EOF
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "docs: fix typo in round_price docstring"
</command>

After that I'd run the plan-completion protocol, delete this plan's workspace, and move to finishing-a-development-branch. The merge and push decisions stay with the partner.

**Message to partner:**

> The plan is complete: all tasks are done and `make test` passes. The whole-branch review returned two findings.
>
> 1. **Fixed:** a docstring typo in `round_price()` ("neerest" → "nearest"). `make test` still passes.
> 2. **Not changed, needs your attention:** the reviewer said `round_price()` should use ROUND_HALF_UP because customers expect half-up rounding. The code uses ROUND_HALF_EVEN, as plan decision D2 (owner, 2026-11-02) requires, to match the ledger system. I kept D2 and recorded a ruling in the ledger. If the owner now wants half-up, the change is one line in `rates/card.py` plus tie-case tests, but it would also break agreement with the ledger system. That decision is the owner's, so please confirm before merge.
>
> Merging and pushing are left to you.
